# Assamese Manuscript Archive (Samaguri Satra, Majuli)

> The digital gateway to Assam's ancient manuscript paintings, Sanchipat folios, Vaishnavite cultural literature, and living mask-making traditions (Mukha Shilpa) of Samaguri Satra, Majuli. A collaborative initiative by Girijananda Chowdhury University (GCU) and Samaguri Satra, funded by the Assam Science Technology and Environment Council (ASTEC) under the ITGA scheme.

## Key Archive Resources
- [Home & Search](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/): Portal overview, curated exhibits, and full catalog search.
- [Collections Catalog](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/collections): Digital folios of ancient Vaishnavite manuscripts, painted texts, and sacred scriptures.
- [Picture Gallery](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/picture-gallery): High-definition visual archive of illuminated manuscripts and Sattriya art.
- [Scholarly Articles](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/knowMore): Curated historical essays on Majuli, Sattra culture, mask making, and Sanchipat preparation.
- [Academic Resources](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/resources): Research bibliography, books, journals, and historical documents.
- [Plan Your Visit](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/visit): Visiting hours (07:00 AM – 05:00 PM, Monday–Sunday), location at Samaguri Satra, entry details (Free), and ferry routes.
- [Audio Guides](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/audioplayer): Trilingual audio commentaries in English, Assamese (অসমীয়া), and Hindi.
- [Project Leadership & Team](https://assammanuscriptarchive.com/team): Academic coordinators (Dr. Nilakshi Goswami, Dr. Shrabani Medhi) and traditional custodians.

## Core Entities & Concepts

### Samaguri Satra (Chamaguri Satra)
Founded in the 17th century in Majuli, Assam, Samaguri Satra is a preeminent Neo-Vaishnavite monastery renowned globally for its unique living tradition of traditional Bhaona mask-making (Mukha Shilpa), championed by Padma Shri awardee Hem Chandra Goswami.

### Assamese Manuscript Paintings
Originating in the 16th century with the Neo-Vaishnavite movement led by saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva and his disciple Madhavdeva, Assamese manuscript paintings illustrate sacred texts like the Bhagavata Purana, Gitagovinda, and Hastividyarnava using vibrant mineral and vegetable pigments.

### Sanchipat Folios
Sanchipat is the indigenous writing surface of Assam, painstakingly prepared from the cured and treated bark of the Sanchi tree (*Aquilaria agallocha* / agarwood). Resistant to humidity, insects, and decay, Sanchipat manuscripts have survived for centuries.

### Mukha Shilpa (Majuli Mask Making)
The traditional art of crafting theatrical masks for Bhaona performances using indigenous bamboo frames (*kamee*), hand-woven cotton cloth, clay from the Brahmaputra River, and organic dyes (*hengul*, *haitaal*). Categorized into Cho-Mukha (large multipart masks), Lotokoi-Mukha (movable-jaw masks), and Mukh-Mukha (face masks).

## Visiting & Contact Details
- **Location**: Samaguri Satra, Majuli / Kaliabor, Assam, India
- **Visiting Hours**: 07:00 AM – 05:00 PM (Monday to Sunday)
- **Admission**: Free (donations and craft purchases support local artisans)
- **Phone**: +91 98765 43210
